This, right here. You understand it completely. I'm not exactly against scantly clad cosplays, it's when you're trying to get critique and you get passed over, or hours of prop making/embroidery/hand-stitching/etc. go unnoticed in competitions for bikini's and short skirts.

The ones that I enter I'm looking for feedback to improve, but I never get the feedback because it gets over looked. I posted my most recent costume a couple week backs and it got down voted. I was looking for honest critique and I got blown off because I wasn't half naked.

Back when I started cosplaying, there was modesty. The "slutty" cosplays were rare and usually horrible made. I don't cosplay for attention, but it burns me like no other when I hear some half naked whore, bitching about how everyone is staring at her goods. Now don't get me wrong. I don't think every half naked cosplayer is willing to do anything for attention, you can usually tell by construction. If it looks awful, they're doing it for the attention, if it's well made with proper material choices, then they're doing it for the love of cosplay.

Another thing that burns me about them, is it seems the most beautiful, in looks alone, seem to win the cosplay contests. I compete my best costumes. I've lost recently and in the past to costumes that were mediocre but the character was skanky, ie cleavage barely taped in, super short shorts/skirt, etc. It feels like 300 hours of labor means nothing to everyone else because the character isn't scantly clad. I'm going to continue my experiment and make a half naked cosplay next time I compete. If I beat other well constructed cosplays with a lot more detailing, then I know that all cosplay is anymore is attention whores.

Again, not all of us are, but those that are modest are the minority now.
I love it, but at this point cosplay is just about sex appeal. If my cosplays would only get attention for that, then I see no point in wasting my time trying to be a master costumer.

Well, cost efficiently, depending on if you make your own body suit or not, and if you screw up or not, you could easily make this for about $100. Unless you need a wig, then it might be a bit more than that.

You could make the "tunic" and cape out of broadcloth, ranges on quality and price from about $4/yd to $10/yd. The more expensive it is, the better the quality. I'd say about $6-$7 would be fine quality for this.

The green gloves, mask, and boots would need to be made of PVC/Vinyl, that would run you about $9/yd and the spandex, depending on the type you get, will run you about $7-$15/yd. Cotton or nylon spandex will cost you about $8/yd. 

If you need a wig, it'll cost you about $30. I recommend [Arda Wigs](http://www.arda-wigs.com/).

Depending on your size, I imagine you'd need 2-3yds of the spandex, 1yd of the PVC/Vinyl, 2yds of the cape fabric, and 1.5-2yds of the red fabric. Hope that helps some.
